scope: Diametral (Brazilian) compression of a bonded-sphere cylinder loaded by two opposed infinite platens. Numerical verification of the apparatus against the analytical Hondros point-load field; no laboratory calibration and no certified ice tensile strength.

reference.name: Hondros (1959) / ASTM D3967 indirect-tension (Brazilian) disc solution

cases.purpose: Elastic stress field only: tensile fracture disabled so the continuum field can be compared with the Hondros solution over a long quasi-static ramp.
Tensile splitting regime: same lattice with a low breaking strain so the diametral tensile stress reaches the bond limit and the crack pattern can be audited.

interpretation_limits: The specimen is a staircase-digitised bonded-sphere cylinder, not a machined rock or ice disc.
Platens are infinite frictionless half-spaces with prescribed constant velocity; the nominal line load is a finite-width contact patch.
The bond model is a central-force (normal only) spring network, so its macroscopic elasticity is not the isotropic continuum assumed by the Hondros solution.
Agreement or disagreement with the analytical field measures the apparatus, not the physical tensile strength of ice.
Peak split stress is a discrete-lattice output and is not a calibrated ice tensile strength.
